slides.hook: Do populist leaders chip away at democracy across the board? No. They go after the rights that let opponents push back: free speech, free association, and a free press.
slides.title: Human rights and populist wrongs: how populist incumbents threaten democracy, 1990–2023
slides.authors: Wade M Cole

slides.title: Populism as a problem of social segregation: socioeconomic composition of personal networks and populist voting
slides.authors: Bernardo Mackenna, Ricardo González, Adolfo Fuentes, and Esteban Muñoz
slides.snippet: Responding to recent calls to understand populism as a problem of social integration, this article proposes a network segregation perspective for the study of populism. Specifically, it theorizes that populist voting is shaped by the socioeconomic composition of individuals’ personal networks.

slides.book_title: Privileged Brotherhoods: Becoming Men at Elite All-Boys Schools

slides.title: Roles in Sociological Field Observations
slides.authors: R. L. Gold

slides.hook: A country hit by disaster does not automatically write a disaster law. Across 204 states from 1960 to 2025, what drives adoption is neighbors passing similar laws, not the hazards.
slides.title: When hazards don’t make law: structural resonance in global disaster-law diffusion, 1960–2025
slides.authors: Maoxin Ye and Daniel P Aldrich

slides.title: Neighborhood change and Black-White segregation: 2000–2020
slides.authors: John R Logan and Liangdi Xu
slides.snippet: This study examines the relationship between neighborhood racial change and metropolitan segregation in 2000–2020. The most surprising finding is that the principal source of declining Black-White segregation has not been Black growth in White neighborhoods.

slides.book_title: Island Time: Theory Groups and the Social Production of Scientific Knowledge

slides.title: Conceptualizing Political Opportunity
slides.authors: D. S. Meyer and D. C. Minkoff

slides.hook: In Italy, left and right parties both passed laws against gender-based violence. The newspapers stayed split: progressives pushed prevention, conservatives pushed punishment.
slides.title: Beneath consensus: political framing of gender-based violence in the Italian press, 2005–2023
slides.authors: Ester Fanelli

slides.title: Life and debt in rural America
slides.authors: Matthew M Brooks and Paromita Sanyal
slides.snippet: Sociology’s growing focus on household debt and wealth has overlooked a potentially salient axis of inequality: rural–urban disparities in the United States. Key facets of rural life indicate a disadvantage (e.g., higher poverty rates, lack of mainstream financial institutions) and a simultaneous advantage (e.g., predominantly White populations, lower cost of living).

slides.book_title: Immigration: How the Past Shapes the Present

slides.title: Housework: Who Did, Does or Will Do It, and How Much Does It Matter?
slides.authors: S. M. Bianchi, L. C. Sayer, M. A. Milkie, and J. P. Robinson

slides.hook: Does discrimination follow you beyond your own neighborhood? Black adults are twice as likely as White adults to report it, and the gap is widest at work, stores, and businesses.
slides.title: Defended neighborhoods, vulnerable routines: routine activities, collective efficacy, and the social ecology of discrimination
slides.authors: Nicolo P Pinchak, Christopher R Browning, Bethany Boettner, J Brandon Carter, and Catherine A Calder

slides.title: Generational imprinting: how political events shape cohorts
slides.authors: Turgut Keskintürk
slides.snippet: Contemporary narratives of generational politics propose that formative experiences produce shared political opinions across an age cohort. In this article, I advance a theory of cohortization to challenge that view, arguing that large–scale political events produce differentiation within cohorts as much as differentiation between them.

slides.book_title: Blame the Intern: On (Not) Breaking into the Creative Economy

slides.title: Anti-Immigrant Prejudice in Europe: Contact, Threat Perception, and Preferences for the Exclusion of Migrants
slides.authors: L. M. McLaren

slides.hook: Gentrification was supposed to break up old segregation. It does for some, but it builds new racial divides in the suburbs and keeps Black and White households apart.
slides.title: Integrating or segregating? Gentrification, the changing city-suburb divide, and black exceptionalism
slides.authors: Jackelyn Hwang, Elizabeth Roberto, Francine I Stephens, and Jacob S Rugh

slides.title: On legacy persistence: historical KKK organizations and racial exclusion in American sundown towns
slides.authors: Kunyuan Qiao, Ashley V Reichelmann, and Matthew O Hunt
slides.snippet: Why do some communities perpetuate historical patterns of racial exclusion while others abandon them? We examine American sundown towns, communities that from the 1890s through the 1960s barred people of color from remaining within their borders after sunset.

slides.title: Feminist Attitudes and Support for Gender Equality: Opinion Change in Women and Men, 1974-1998
slides.authors: C. I. Bolzendahl and D. J. Myers

slides.hook: A holiday looks like a neutral date on the calendar. In rural China, Spring Festival becomes a marriage market where bachelors get audited and ranked before migrants scatter again.
slides.title: Festivalized marriage as a Time Threshold: Spring Festival bottlenecks, Qualification Audits, and escalating entry standards in rural China
slides.authors: Yong Yu, Keke Qin, Wenzhao Huang, and Shishi Tang

slides.title: Enduring links: mental health effects of ex-partner’s life events among separated parents
slides.authors: Philipp Dierker, Mine Kühn, Sanna Kailaheimo-Björkqvist, and Mikko Myrskylä
slides.snippet: Union dissolutions between parents do not necessarily end interdependencies between them. This study examines whether life events of ex-partners with a shared child affect each other’s mental health, extending life course theory on linked lives beyond intact families.

slides.book_title: An Elite Education: How Privilege Is Produced in a Private School

slides.title: Narrations of non-motherhood: how context shapes what it means to be childless in the United States and Japan
slides.authors: Holly Hummer
slides.snippet: In our era of low fertility rates, much research has examined factors behind delayed childbearing and childlessness. While scholars emphasize the role of macro-level context in constraining reproductive decision-making, less attention has been paid to how context shapes what it means, subjectively, to remain childless today.

slides.hook: Across the 20th century, words for stupidity drifted toward men. Not because people called men dumb, but because those words moved into harsher, more combative company.
slides.title: Explaining gendered language through embedding approximation: how “stupid” became a man’s word
slides.authors: Yutong Zhu

slides.title: Curricular-credential decoupling: how schools respond to college and career readiness policy
slides.authors: Matt S Giani, Madison E Andrews, Tasneem Sultana, and Fortunato N Medrano
slides.snippet: This study examines schools’ college and career readiness (CCR) policy responses through the lens of decoupling. We investigate how high schools have jointly implemented career and technical education (CTE) and industry-based certifications (IBCs), and whether there is evidence of curricular-credential decoupling via misalignment between the subject areas of students’ CTE coursework and IBC completion.

slides.book_title: The Religious Left: What It Does and How It Can Do Better

slides.title: The global rise in children’s attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder prevalence: a macro-sociological explanation
slides.authors: Irem Tuncer-Ebetürk, Jessica Kim, and Yasemin Nuhoğlu Soysal
slides.snippet: In the past three decades, the global diagnosis rate of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has grown drastically. While existing sociological studies demonstrate the complexity of ADHD diagnoses and treatment in specific national contexts, their ability to explain ADHD’s global growth is limited.

slides.hook: Whiteness pays multiracial young adults the usual social wages. But those wages come bundled with a racial tax that monoracial Whites never face.
slides.title: Multiracial young adults’ experiences of Whiteness as a wage and tax
slides.authors: Monica Heilman

slides.title: Occupational hazard and political segregation in the US labor market
slides.authors: Ray Tsai Fang
slides.snippet: The tendency for liberals and conservatives to cluster in different occupations significantly impacts society, yet the factors that contribute to this type of segregation remain incompletely understood. Bridging research from cultural and cognitive psychology, I develop a theory describing how occupational environments can shape people’s political ideologies, thereby contributing to political segregation in the labor market.

slides.book_title: The Story of a Generation: Life Course Pathways of the Class of ‘73

slides.title: Colonial legacy and contemporary civil violence: a global study from 1960 to 2018
slides.authors: Christopher Kollmeyer
slides.snippet: This study assesses whether the legacy of colonialism continues to influence patterns of civil violence in the contemporary era. A large and established quantitative literature attributes civil violence to low levels of economic development and limited political rights, but few quantitative studies consider whether colonial legacy plays an enduring role in such conflicts.

slides.authors: Guido Salza and Moris Triventi
slides.snippet: This paper examines whether evaluations of primary-school characteristics vary across national and social contexts. Using a factorial survey experiment with more than 2500 respondents in the United States, Germany, and Italy, participants evaluated hypothetical schools differing in six attributes.

slides.title: Human rights and populist wrongs: how populist incumbents threaten democracy, 1990–2023
slides.authors: Wade M Cole
slides.snippet: This paper leverages variation in respect for human rights to intervene in ongoing debates over the consequences of populism for democracy. Compiling data for 103 democratic countries between 1990 and 2023, and using a novel cross-national classification of populist leaders and parties, I examine the relationships between left-wing, centrist, and right-wing populist incumbency and 18 measures of civil, political, and social rights.

slides.title: Working from home among older adults in the UK: examining its link to labor market exit intentions and expected retirement age
slides.authors: Yanan Zhang, Sarah Harper, Senhu Wang, and Bing Gong
slides.snippet: Prolonging work life has been widely discussed in countries facing population aging. We examine the association between working from home (WFH) and both the labor market exit intentions and expected retirement age among the older workforce in the UK, utilizing data from the harmonized British Household Panel Survey (BHPS) and the UK Household Longitudinal Survey (UKHLS), covering the period from September 1998 to May 2020.

slides.hook: When more people earn college degrees, do graduates land jobs that use their major? It depends: matches improve for economics and math, but worsen for the sciences and philosophy.
slides.title: University expansion, academic fields, and the match between the degree and the job
slides.authors: Jonathan Horowitz and Sagi Ramaj

slides.title: Do caring fathers earn less? Earnings consequences of fathers’ parental leave use
slides.authors: Corinna Frodermann, Ann-Christin Bächmann, and Andreas Filser
slides.snippet: In many Western societies, policy efforts seek to increase fathers’ involvement in parental leave, yet many fathers remain reluctant due to concerns about earnings consequences. Despite these concerns, the consequences of parental leave and their underlying mechanisms remain understudied.

slides.hook: Does a freer market always punish short-term workers? In China, not in the state sector, where marketization shrinks the pay penalty for temporary jobs. In private firms it grows.
slides.title: Job precarity and earnings inequality in contemporary China
slides.authors: Zhipeng Zhou

slides.hook: Highways were routed through neighborhoods the government had already graded red. Eighty years on, those blocks still carry the heaviest traffic emissions, whoever lives there now.
slides.title: Paving the way: redlining and contemporary transportation emissions in US cities
slides.authors: Rachel McKane and Patrick Trent Greiner
